title: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19)
description: This dataset comprises multi-night ear-EEG and polysomnography (PSG) recordings collected between 2018 and 2020 to develop and validate ear-EEG as a home-based sleep monitoring platform. Twenty subjects were recorded across four nights with partial PSG, ear-EEG, and actigraphy, while ten of these subjects continued for an additional twelve nights using only ear-EEG, actigraphy, and a single EOG electrode. Supplementary behavioral data include nightly comfort questionnaires, sleep diaries, and actigraphy recordings, providing a rich resource for studying sleep physiology and wearable EEG signal quality.
methods_description: Subjects slept at home wearing ear-EEG electrodes alongside partial PSG (EEG, EOG, chin EMG) for the first four nights, and a subset continued for twelve additional nights with ear-EEG, actigraphy, and a single EOG electrode. Actigraphy was recorded with wrist-worn GENEactiv devices measuring 3-axis acceleration, temperature, light, and button presses. Each night, participants completed a comfort questionnaire and a sleep diary, and performed an electrode quality test involving jaw clenching, eye movements, and open/closed eyes. Data were minimally preprocessed; faulty electrodes with signal leakage were identified and set to NaN in the .set files.
